models_evaluated: two previously validated AI pipelines generating five cTIL scores (locked models)

links.outcome: Prognostic performance of locked AI TIL models on independent multisite trial data
links.effect: Two cTIL models deployed without retraining gave significant prognostic information and improved 5-year AUC over clinicopathological variables alone; cTIL did not add beyond sTIL.
links.quote: Two cTIL models deployed entirely without retraining or modification provided statistically significant prognostic information and improved risk discrimination compared with clinicopathological variables alone in this large, platform-based, independent validation study.

links.outcome: Independent, masked external evaluation of AI models by assessors independent of developers
links.effect: Independent masked deployment of locked models found modest correlation with pathologist sTILs (r 0.375-0.473) and significant prognostic association in unadjusted-for-sTIL models.
links.quote: We independently evaluated two previously validated AI pipelines that generate five computationally assessed tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte (cTIL) scores by masked, independent deployment of locked models.

screen.reason: This is an independent external validation study of locked computational pathology AI models (cTIL scores) against pathologist scores and clinical outcomes across prospective trial cohorts, evaluating model prognostic performance rather than a specific deployment guardrail or workflow practice.
